title: Double-tap Withdraw: 'you can't go negative'
topic: A wallet check that only works one click at a time
blurb: The user has $100 and mashes Withdraw $80 twice. The AI says the balance check makes that impossible.
prompt: An AI wrote this Node.js withdrawal handler for a wallet app. A user with $100 double-taps 'Withdraw $80'. Find the bug before it ships.

segments.label: L6
segments.text: return { ok: true, balance: balance - amount };

conclusion: AI summary: We check `balance < amount` before writing, so the balance can never go negative. Ship it.

flaws.original: const updated = await db.atomicDebitIfEnough(userId, amount); // atomic conditional update / transaction

diagnosis_choices.label: Race condition (TOCTOU): two concurrent calls both read $100, pass L4, and overwrite with $20 — withdrawing $160.
JavaScript is single-threaded, so `await` blocks all other requests until `withdraw` finishes.
`balance - amount` uses string concatenation instead of subtraction in JS.
Missing `try/catch` around `setBalance` causes the balance to double.

fix_choices.label: Use an atomic DB update/transaction (e.g. `UPDATE ... SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ? AND balance >= ?`).
Remove `await` on line 5 so the write happens synchronously.
Re-read `db.getBalance` a second time before `setBalance` without a lock.

flaws.explanation: Each `await` yields back to the event loop. Two simultaneous $80 withdrawals both read `balance = 100`, both pass the check, and both write `20` — letting the user spend $160 from a $100 wallet.
flaws.why_tempting: Developers assume 'Node.js is single-threaded' means no race conditions, forgetting that async I/O interleaves between `await` points.
flaws.catch_rule: Whenever you see `read -> await -> check -> await -> write` on shared money or quota, demand an atomic conditional update or DB transaction.
flaws.hint: Imagine both taps pausing after they read the balance, before either one writes.

practice.problem: A drop has `left = 1`. Two fans hit Buy at the same instant using `get` then `set(left - 1)`. What happens?
practice.answer: Both read `1`, both succeed, and two people just bought the last item.

clean_conclusion: The database checks and deducts in one step, so two taps can't both sneak through.
